### Health Insurance Open Enrollment Survey: 57% of Americans Say Picking a Health Plan Is Stressful


October 28, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s204.q4cdn.com/837903328/files/doc_news/Health-Insurance-Open-Enrollment-Survey-57-of-Americans-Say-Picking-a-Health-Plan-Is-Stressful-2026.pdf)


***84% of Americans say it feels like health insurance is designed to be*** ***confusing on purpose***


***48% say they've used artificial intelligence (AI) to review their insurance options***


***78% say healthcare affordability is a top-three voting issue for them in the upcoming midterm election***


INDIANAPOLIS


, Oct. 28, 2026


/PRNewswire/ -- With tens of millions of Americans selecting 2027 health insurance plans during the fall open enrollment period,[new research](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4808101-1&h=3522624976&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.ehealthinsurance.com%2F_ir%2F68%2F20269%2F119fe42637d71e14a30f7ac622f8d91c%2FeHealth_Open_Enrollment_2026_Survey_Report.pdf&a=new+research) from[eHealth](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4808101-1&h=4254821382&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.ehealthinsurance.com%2F&a=eHealth) (Nasdaq: EHTH) reveals how stressful the process of picking a plan is for most consumers, while highlighting the growing role of AI in healthcare.


Based on the survey of over 1,000 Americans, the new report from eHealth, a leading private online health insurance marketplace, found:


- 84% of Americans feel like the health insurance system is intentionally designed to be confusing.
- 57% of Americans consider open enrollment season stressful, while 53% say choosing a health plan is as bad as, or worse than, doing their federal taxes.
- 71% of Americans admit they've stuck with the same health plan for multiple years just to avoid the trouble of researching their options.
- 78% of likely voters say healthcare affordability is a top-three issue for them in the upcoming midterm elections.


"Health benefits open enrollment is a stressful time for many Americans, given the complexity of reviewing, understanding and selecting the right insurance plan based on individual needs and preferences," said[Derrick Duke](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4808101-1&h=2568514499&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.ehealthinsurance.com%2Fexperts%2Fderrick-duke&a=Derrick+Duke) , CEO of[eHealth](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4808101-1&h=4254821382&u=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.ehealthinsurance.com%2F&a=eHealth) . "This report highlights the need for improved consumer education and support, as making informed coverage decisions can improve access to quality care, contribute to well-being and protect consumers from unexpected medical costs."


Additional highlights from the report:


**On AI's role in healthcare and insurance**


- 48% of Americans have used an artificial intelligence (AI) tool to review their health insurance options.
- 41% of Americans say it will be 10 years or longer before an AI tool can replace a doctor for medical advice, including 30% who say that will never be the case.
- 22% say AI can already replace doctors for medical advice.
- 67% of Americans who have used AI for medical advice admit the guidance they received has sometimes been incorrect.
- 82% of Americans would support a law that requires a human to review any medical claim that was denied by an AI tool.


**On barriers to accessing medical care**


- 58% of insured Americans have skipped or delayed medical care due to concerns about out-of-pocket costs.
- 46% of insured Americans have skipped or delayed medical care due to uncertainty about their coverage.


**On Affordable Care Act (ACA) and employer-sponsored plans**


- 68% of ACA plan enrollees are worried they won't be able to find affordable coverage for 2027.
- 36% of ACA plan enrollees say their current plan is unaffordable for them.
- 37% of ACA plan enrollees say their government premium subsidies were reduced from 2025 to 2026.
- 43% of all Americans say they are familiar with Custom Health Options and Individual Care Expense (CHOICE) Arrangements, formerly ICHRA.
- 77% of people with employer-based coverage wish their employers offered a broader selection of health insurance plans to choose from.


Read the[full report](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4808101-1&h=1445963919&u=https%3A%2F%2Fnews.ehealthinsurance.com%2F_ir%2F68%2F20269%2F119fe42637d71e14a30f7ac622f8d91c%2FeHealth_Open_Enrollment_2026_Survey_Report.pdf&a=full+report) .


eHealth's report is based on a census-balanced survey of more than 1,000 Americans drawn from the general population. The survey was conducted in October 2026 through a third-party survey tool. The margin of error is +/- 3%.
